CHANGELOG (`15.1.0-next.1`): `CanLoad guards in the Router are deprecated. Use CanMatch instead.` The deprecation comment at [`router_module.ts` line 41–44](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/angular-angular@27da7338ea8f3bf5336d77ed1877cfa6a1974d52/-/blob/packages/router/src/router_module.ts?L41-L44) (`// TODO(atscott): ... ### 8c. `providedIn: NgModule` / `providedIn: 'any'` deprecations

CHANGELOG (`15.0.0`): both deprecated in the core DI system. The deprecation messages are evidence of in-progress cleanup of confusing API surface.

### 8d. `ReflectiveInjector` legacy code

[`packages/core/src/di/reflective_injector.ts`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/angular-angular@27da7338ea8f3bf5336d77ed1877cfa6a1974d52/-/blob/packages/core/src/di/reflective_injector.ts), `reflective_key.ts`, `reflective_provider.ts`, `reflective_errors.ts` — the full View Engine reflective DI subsystem is retained for compatibility but lives alongside the Ivy `R3Injector`. These files are cleanup-deferred legacy code; no active development is evidenced here.

## 9. Test Generation

The `packages/core/test/` tree is extensive (18 subdirectories, 14 top-level spec files). Notable sub-directories include `test/acceptance/`, `test/render3/`, `test/di/`, and `test/bundling/`. The `packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/extended/test/` and `packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/testing/` directories contain test infrastructure specific to the extended template diagnostic checks.

**Ambiguity:** It cannot be determined from the snapshot alone whether any test files were generated (e.g., by a script or AI tool) versus hand-written. All test files follow idiomatic Angular testing patterns (Jasmine `describe`/`it`, `TestBed`, etc.) consistent with hand-authorship. This category is therefore **present in structure** but **not clearly evidenced as a distinct engineering task shape** distinct from ordinary feature test authorship at this revision.

## Taxonomy Refinement Proposal

The standard eight categories cover all observed task shapes. One refinement is warranted:

> **Proposed addition: `api-deprecation-surface`** — a distinct task shape that is neither pure cleanup (which removes code) nor documentation (which adds text), but the deliberate act of annotating existing public API symbols with `@deprecated` + migration path + CHANGELOG prose + (optionally) a paired schematic. This pattern appears at least six times in this snapshot (`RouterLinkWithHref`, `createNgModuleRef`, `canLoad`, `relativeLinkResolution`, `providedIn: NgModule`, `Injector.get` bitfield). It straddles cleanup (intent), documentation (mechanism), and occasionally boilerplate schematic (automation). Merging it into "cleanup" loses the fact that the API is still live; merging into "documentation" loses the programmatic migration tooling. A `deprecation-lifecycle` sub-tag within cleanup would disambiguate without requiring a new top-level category.

## 3. Refactor

### 3a. Router internals decomposed from `Router` class into `NavigationTransitions`

[`packages/router/src/navigation_transition.ts`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/angular-angular@27da7338ea8f3bf5336d77ed1877cfa6a1974d52/-/blob/packages/router/src/navigation_transition.ts) is a new injectable that holds the full RxJS pipeline for navigation. `router_module.ts` imports `NavigationTransitions` and delegates to it; `router.ts` no longer owns this state. This is a textbook extract-class refactor enabling the `provideRouter`-based approach to work without `RouterModule`. The CHANGELOG deprecation note (`router writable properties`) in `15.1.0-next.0` signals that previously-public `Router` fields are being moved into configuration — a refactor in progress.

### 3b. `RouterLinkWithHref` merged into `RouterLink`

The RouterLink contains the code from the RouterLinkWithHref to handle elements with href attributes.` The schematic in `router-link-with-href/` automates the mechanical source-code change — the underlying implementation merge is a refactor (consolidating two directives into one).

The `packages/core/test/` tree is extensive (18 subdirectories, 14 top-level spec files). Notable sub-directories include `test/acceptance/`, `test/render3/`, `test/di/`, and `test/bundling/`. **Ambiguity:** It cannot be determined from the snapshot alone whether any test files were generated (e.g., by a script or AI tool) versus hand-written. All test files follow idiomatic Angular testing patterns (Jasmine `describe`/`it`, `TestBed`, etc.) consistent with hand-authorship. No generation markers, generator comments, or templated test boilerplate patterns are visible. This category is therefore **present in structure** but **not clearly evidenced as a distinct engineering task shape** distinct from ordinary feature test authorship at this revision.

## Taxonomy Refinement Proposal

The standard eight categories cover all observed task shapes. One refinement is warranted:

> **Proposed addition: `api-deprecation-surface`** — a distinct task shape that is neither pure cleanup (which removes code) nor documentation (which adds text), but the deliberate act of annotating existing public API symbols with `@deprecated` + migration path + CHANGELOG prose + (optionally) a paired schematic. This pattern appears at least six times in this snapshot (`RouterLinkWithHref`, `createNgModuleRef`, `canLoad`, `relativeLinkResolution`, `providedIn: NgModule`, `Injector.get` bitfield). It straddles cleanup (intent), documentation (mechanism), and occasionally boilerplate schematic (automation). Merging it into "cleanup" loses the fact that the API is still live; merging into "documentation" loses the programmatic migration tooling. A `deprecation-lifecycle` sub-tag within cleanup would disambiguate without requiring a new top-level category.
